title: Higher-width graded cokernels of close finite free complexes
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq B$ an ideal, and $L,M,F$ finite free $B$-modules, meaning isomorphic to $B^d$ for finite integers $d\geq0$. Let $r,r':L\to M$ and $p,p':M\to F$ be $B$-linear maps satisfying $\operatorname{im}r=\ker p$ and $p'r'=0$. For every module $V$ set $I^jV=V$ when $j\leq0$, and for $j>0$ let $I^jV$ be the submodule generated by $av$ with $a\in I^j$ and $v\in V$. Suppose $c\geq0$ satisfies, for every $j\geq c$, $\operatorname{im}r\cap I^jM\subseteq r(I^{j-c}L)$ and $\operatorname{im}p\cap I^jF\subseteq p(I^{j-c}M)$. Let $n\geq c$ and assume $(r-r')(L)\subseteq I^{n+1}M$ and $(p-p')(M)\subseteq I^{n+1}F$. Put $a=n+1-c\geq1$. Then for every $q\in\mathbf Z$,
$$I^{q+a}F+(I^qF\cap\operatorname{im}p)=I^{q+a}F+(I^qF\cap\operatorname{im}p').$$
Consequently the identity of $F$ induces an isomorphism of graded $G_a(B)$-modules $G_a(\operatorname{coker}p)\cong G_a(\operatorname{coker}p')$, where $G_a(V)=\bigoplus_{q\in\mathbf Z}I^qV/I^{q+a}V$ and $G_a(B)$ has multiplication induced from $B$. If $F=B$, the same isomorphism is an isomorphism of graded $G_a(B)$-algebras, using the quotient-ring structures on both cokernels. No assumption that $I$ is in the Jacobson radical is made, and no exactness of the perturbed complex is asserted.

proof.text: As $n\geq c$, the map differences take values in $I^{c+1}$ times their targets. Fix $j\geq c$ and $x\in M$ with $y=p'(x)\in I^jF$, and put $k=j-c$. Inductively construct $x_t\in I^tM$, for $0\leq t\leq k$, such that $p'(x_t)=y$ and $x-x_t\in\operatorname{im}r'$. Start with $x_0=x$; both claims hold because $I^0M=M$ and $x-x_0=0$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph: finite adjustment and the following preimage inclusion. Only this finite argument is used, not the later perturbed-exactness conclusion.

proof.text: For a linear map $u:V\to W$ satisfying $u(V)\subseteq I^NW$, linearity gives $u(I^tV)\subseteq I^{N+t}W$ for $t\geq0$: expand $v=\sum_i a_iv_i$ with $a_i\in I^t$, and expand each $u(v_i)$ with coefficients in $I^N$. The resulting coefficient products belong to $I^{N+t}$. In the induction use $N=c+1$; in the graded comparison use $N=n+1$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph: finite adjustment and the following preimage inclusion. Only this finite argument is used, not the later perturbed-exactness conclusion.

proof.text: Suppose $t<k$ and $x_t$ has been constructed. Then $j\geq t+c+1$, so $p(x_t)=y+(p-p')(x_t)\in I^{t+c+1}F$ by step 2. The assumed bound for $p$, at exponent $t+c+1\geq c$, gives $v\in I^{t+1}M$ with $p(v)=p(x_t)$. Thus $x_t-v\in\ker p=\operatorname{im}r$, and we may choose $b\in L$ with $r(b)=x_t-v\in I^tM$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph: finite adjustment and the following preimage inclusion. Only this finite argument is used, not the later perturbed-exactness conclusion.

proof.text: If $t\geq c$, the assumed bound for $r$, at exponent $t$, lets us replace $b$ by an element of $I^{t-c}L$ with that same image. If $t<c$, keep the chosen $b$. Put $x_{t+1}=x_t-r'(b)=v+(r-r')(b)$. In the first case step 2 puts the last term in $I^{t-c+c+1}M=I^{t+1}M$; in the second it is in $I^{c+1}M\subseteq I^{t+1}M$. Hence $x_{t+1}\in I^{t+1}M$.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph: finite adjustment and the following preimage inclusion. Only this finite argument is used, not the later perturbed-exactness conclusion.

proof.text: The zero-product $p'r'=0$ gives $p'(x_{t+1})=p'(x_t)=y$. Also $x-x_{t+1}=(x-x_t)+r'(b)\in\operatorname{im}r'$. This proves both inductive invariants and completes the finite induction. At $t=k$ it gives $y=p'(x_k)$ with $x_k\in I^{j-c}M$. Since $j,y$ were arbitrary, $\operatorname{im}p'\cap I^jF\subseteq p'(I^{j-c}M)$ for every $j\geq c$. When $j=c$, $k=0$ and the base case suffices. No infinite intersection or Jacobson-radical hypothesis was used.

source.place: Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph: finite adjustment and the following preimage inclusion. Only this finite argument is used, not the later perturbed-exactness conclusion.

proof.text: Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$ and first suppose $q\leq c$. If $y=p(x)\in I^qF$, then $y-p'(x)\in I^{n+1}F\subseteq I^{q+a}F\subseteq I^qF$, since $n+1=c+a\geq q+a$ and $a\geq1$. Hence $p'(x)\in I^qF\cap\operatorname{im}p'$ and $y\in I^{q+a}F+(I^qF\cap\operatorname{im}p')$. Interchanging $p,p'$ proves the reverse inclusion, using the negative of the same difference. Adding the common summand $I^{q+a}F$ gives the asserted equality. All inclusions remain valid with the stated convention for nonpositive exponents.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 4.5(iii)-(iv), printed pp.39-41; preliminary finite adjustment from Stacks Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Suppose $q>c$. For $y=p(x)\in I^qF$, the assumed bound supplies $v\in I^{q-c}M$ with $p(v)=y$. Step 2 gives $p(v)-p'(v)\in I^{n+1+q-c}F=I^{q+a}F\subseteq I^qF$. Thus $p'(v)\in I^qF\cap\operatorname{im}p'$ represents $y$ modulo $I^{q+a}F$. For the reverse inclusion use the bound for $p'$ obtained in step 5: write $y'=p'(v')$ with $v'\in I^{q-c}M$, and the same difference estimate shows that $p(v')$ represents $y'$ modulo $I^{q+a}F$. The two inclusions, after adding $I^{q+a}F$, prove the equality in every remaining degree.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 4.5(iii)-(iv), printed pp.39-41; preliminary finite adjustment from Stacks Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: For $U=\operatorname{im}p$, put $Q=F/U$. The quotient map $\pi:F\to Q$ sends $I^qF$ onto $I^qQ$, by expanding finite sums (and surjectivity for $q\leq0$). The map $I^qF\to I^qQ/I^{q+a}Q$ has kernel $I^{q+a}F+(I^qF\cap U)$: if $\pi(x)\in I^{q+a}Q$, choose $z\in I^{q+a}F$ with $\pi(z)=\pi(x)$; then $x-z\in I^qF\cap U$. The converse follows by applying $\pi$. Therefore sending a class of $x\in I^qF$ to the class of $\pi(x)$ is a bijective linear map from the quotient by this kernel onto $I^qQ/I^{q+a}Q$. Repeat with $U'=\operatorname{im}p'$. The equal kernels proved above give the required identity-induced degreewise bijections.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 4.5(iii)-(iv), printed pp.39-41; preliminary finite adjustment from Stacks Tag 07VE, lemma-approximate-complex, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Take the direct sum of these degreewise bijections: on a finite homogeneous sum apply the corresponding bijection to each component, with componentwise inverses. For homogeneous $b\in I^sB$ and $x\in I^qF$, either composite with scalar multiplication is represented by $bx\in I^{s+q}F$. Thus the isomorphism is $G_a(B)$-linear and preserves degrees. Multiplication is well defined even for negative degrees: $I^uI^v\subseteq I^{u+v}$ for all integers $u,v$, since $\max(u,0)+\max(v,0)\geq\max(u+v,0)$; this also handles changed representatives in denominator powers. If $F=B$, the images of $p$ and $p'$ are ideals. Products of classes represented by $x,y\in B$ are represented by $xy$ in both quotients, and the unit is represented by $1$ in degree zero. The isomorphism therefore also preserves multiplication and the unit, proving the graded algebra assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q153-6f8fd8f88 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and accept it with no changes. There are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged; the delivery's nine elementary steps are fully written out. Sources checked: ILO III Definition 4.4, Proposition 4.5 (i)-(iv) with its proof on printed pp.39-41, and Theorem 5.1 (5.a), which is how the caller uses it; also Stacks 07VE lemma-approximate-complex (first proof paragraph and the displayed preimage inclusion) and 07VF. Steps 1-5 are the finite adjustment of 07VE with the induction claim, base and step stated. I checked both cases of step 4 (t>=c with b in I^{t-c}L, and t<c where the error lies in I^{c+1}M, inside I^{t+1}M). Together these steps prove the transferred Artin-Rees bound for p' (ILO 4.5(i)) without any Jacobson-radical hypothesis. Step 6 is the q<=c case, using n+1=c+a>=q+a. Step 7 is the q>c case, with error exponent n+1+q-c=q+a; its reverse inclusion uses the bound from step 5, which is exactly what ILO's 'par symetrie' needs. Step 8 identifies the quotient kernel by lifting z in I^{q+a}F. Step 9 checks the G_a(B)-linearity, the integer-power products and the algebra structure for F=B. The statement rightly leaves out 4.5(ii): over B=kxk with I=kx0, r=id, r'=(0,1), p=p'=0 and c=n=0, the perturbed complex is not exact. Edge cases tested: I=0, I=B, j=c, a=1, q<=-a, q=c and q=c+1, and k[t] with p=t^c against p'=t^c(1+t^a). Dropping p'r'=0 breaks step 5. Duplicates: lem-sfb-perturbed-image-artin-rees-bound assumes I is in every maximal ideal, so it cannot be cited; lem-sfb-adic-relation-matrix-initial-ideals is the local, width-one case; the parent lem-per-gabber-graded-model-approximation cites the item in step 6 with F=B, which matches the statement. There is no repair note or re-split order, there are no tool_uses, and the item cites no node, so there is no route issue. The only stmt_dep, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, is correct, and searches of all three kinds are recorded. Details are in review.md.
